AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Digit ratio (2D:4D) is fixed in utero and affected by fetal sex steroids. It has been proposed as a putative biomarker of certain hormone- related adult life traits and diseases. Several evidence suggest that 2D:4D ratio may correlate with cardiovascular disease risk (e.g., coronary artery disease).

AbstractText.Label: AIMS
AbstractText.content: To investigate whether there is a possible relationship between digit ratio (especially 2D:4D ratio) and coronary artery disease (CAD), and age at CAD in north Chinese women.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Photographs of the two hands of 303 females (controls: 194; patients: 109) were collected. Left hand, right hand and right minus left hand (Dr-l) digit ratio were analyzed and compared.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The mean values of digit ratio in patients with CAD were lower than controls for each hand. Significant differences of 2D:4D (left and right hand: P<0.01), 2D:5D (left hand: P<0.01; right hand: P<0.05) and 3D:4D (left hand: P<0.01) were found between two groups. There were no associations between 2D:4D ratio and age at CAD on both hands.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Decreased digit ratio (especially 2D:4D ratio) may suggest a higher prenatal testosterone (lower prenatal oestrogen) exposure in north Chinese women with coronary artery disease.
